name: MusicGen
tagline: Meta's text-to-music model. **Melody** models follow a tune you give them; regular models can **continue** audio you give them.
disk: small 2 GB · medium 6 GB · melody 6 GB · large 13 GB

params.name: model
params.help: Any MusicGen model id from Hugging Face works, including fine-tunes. Type one in.

params.name: prompt
params.default: dark minimal techno, 126 bpm, rolling acid bassline, crisp hats, warehouse reverb

params.name: audio
params.label: Input audio (optional)
params.help: Melody models: follows the melody/harmony of this. Other models: continues from it.

params.name: duration
params.help: Seconds. Over 30s, non-melody models extend in windows.

params.name: guidance_scale
params.help: How strongly to follow the prompt. Higher = more literal, less varied.

params.name: audio_start
params.help: Use the input audio from this second…

params.name: audio_length
params.help: …for this many seconds (continuation prompt / melody length).

params.name: keep_input
params.help: Continuation: keep the input audio at the start of the result.

params.name: extend_overlap
params.help: For songs over 30s: seconds of context carried into each new window.

notes:
- **Melody conditioning:** pick a `melody` model, drop in your track or a hummed idea, and describe the new style.
- **Continuation:** pick a non-melody model, drop in a loop, and it carries on from where your audio ends.
- Prompts work best as comma-separated tags: genre, bpm, instruments, mood, production style.
- Use **Runs** with a fixed seed to explore variations.
